sections.name: Banana and Banana Bunch
sections.card:
Summary: A Banana is a peel you drop on the track, and a kart that runs over it spins out. The Banana Bunch puts five Bananas in a trail behind your kart.
Uses: Each Banana in the Bunch can be thrown whenever you choose, and while the trail sits behind your kart it also stops items that would hit you. Only one banana can be dropped at a time.
Tips: A Banana trailing behind your kart protects you from homing Red Shells, and does so less well against Green Shells.

sections.name: Green Shell and Triple Green Shells
sections.card:
Summary: A Green Shell travels in a straight line toward the racer you aim at, and a racer it hits is flipped over several times. Triple Green Shells put three shells in a ring around your kart.
Uses: A Green Shell ricochets off walls repeatedly until it hits a target or is destroyed, and holding the stick backwards fires it backwards. With the triple, you throw the shells one at a time or keep them as a shield against items and projectiles, and the ring can also ram other karts.
Tips: Triple shells cannot be fired backwards, unlike a single one, and spinning around your kart makes them a little harder to aim. Computer racers do not get Green Shells in this game.

sections.name: Red Shell and Triple Red Shells
sections.card:
Summary: A Red Shell automatically targets the racer immediately ahead of you. Triple Red Shells put three Red Shells in a ring around your kart.
Uses: A Red Shell can only go forward, but it keeps to the road to reach its target, and a wall destroys it. With the triple, you throw the shells one at a time or keep them as a shield against incoming items.
Tips: Only in this game can a Fake Item Box stop a Red Shell coming at you. A Banana held behind your kart also guards against Red Shells.

sections.name: Spiny Shell (blue)
sections.card:
Summary: The Spiny Shell is the rarest item. It travels along the ground with a siren sound and flings the racer in the lead into the air.
Uses: It goes only forward, never back, and crosses gaps and jumps without trouble. Any other racer in its way is flung into the air too. If you fire it from first place, it turns around and hits you.
Tips: An obstacle in its path destroys it, and so does an invincible racer, whom it fails to hurt. A shell that meets an invisible leader goes straight through, though it can circle the course once more and still hit them later.
Tips: Two sideways Item Boxes, one under the hot-air balloon on Luigi Raceway and one atop the large rock on Koopa Troopa Beach, always give a Spiny Shell whatever your place.

sections.name: Mushroom and Triple Mushrooms
sections.card:
Summary: A Mushroom gives you a short speed boost. Triple Mushrooms give you three boosts that you use one at a time.
Uses: Run into another racer during a Mushroom boost and they spin out. When the last of the three Mushrooms is used, the triple's effect ends.
Tips: In Bowser's Castle, boost with a Mushroom or use a Star and you can cross the grass in the first courtyard, skipping its first two turns.

sections.name: Super Mushroom (Golden Mushroom)
sections.card:
Summary: What later games call the Golden Mushroom is the Super Mushroom here, a yellow-capped mushroom whose icon has a glow behind it.
Uses: Its boosts have no cap, but only until the effect runs out.
Tips: In the item window, look for the yellow-capped mushroom with the glow behind it.

sections.name: Super Star
sections.card:
Summary: For about ten seconds a Super Star makes you invincible and lets you pass through items, obstacles on the course and other racers.
Uses: You also drive about a third faster and can go off-road unhindered. A racer you hit flips over and loses the item they are holding.
Tips: If you hit a wall hard enough that your character exclaims, the Star ends at once.
Tips: A Star that is running when Lightning strikes keeps you from shrinking, and a Star destroys a Spiny Shell without hurting you.

sections.name: Lightning (Thunder Bolt)
sections.card:
Summary: Lightning, called the Thunder Bolt in this game, shrinks every other racer, which slows them down and lets other karts flatten them.
Uses: A shrunk racer loses nothing it is holding, but a Mushroom, Super Star or Boo sitting in its item window can no longer be used. Karts that kept their size can run over the smaller ones and flatten them, and if two shrunk racers collide, both are crushed.
Tips: A Super Star or a Boo that is already running when the bolt strikes keeps you from shrinking. While Lightning is in effect a sound like a tiny alarm plays.

sections.name: Fake Item Box
sections.card:
Summary: A trap that looks like a normal Item Box, but its question mark is upside down. A kart that hits one is blasted into the air.
Uses: Held behind your kart it stops incoming shells the way a Banana does, but it cannot be thrown ahead, and one set down in midair stays floating.
Tips: Look at the question mark when you drive up to a box: the fake one's is upside down.

sections.name: Boo
sections.card:
Summary: The Boo item makes you invisible and invincible for a short time while it steals an item from an opponent.
Uses: While it lasts you pass straight through items, obstacles on the course and other racers. Computer racers use Boos too, but their Boos do not steal items.
Tips: A Boo that is already running when Lightning strikes keeps you from shrinking, but once you are shrunk you cannot use a Boo from your item window.

sections.name: Thwomp
sections.card:
Summary: Blue stone blocks in Bowser's Castle that try to flatten racers who drive under them. Some slam down from the air, and some slide from side to side on the ground.
Weak points: Thwomps are obstacles in the course, not something you fight: the ones that drop try to flatten anyone racing beneath them, and the sliding ones try to bump racers on the ground. A Super Star lets you drive through course obstacles.
Tips: The first corridor after the courtyard holds four Thwomps; they drift about overhead and then drop onto the track. A pair at the start of the next corridor tracks you, drops, and goes back to where it began, and the row at the far end drops one at a time: one Thwomp in 50cc, two in 100cc, three in 150cc.
Tips: Two Thwomps in a later room stay at ground level and slide from side to side. The slightly larger green Thwomp locked up at the end of the first corridor shakes and laughs when you go near.

sections.name: Train (Kalimari Desert)
sections.card:
Summary: Two trains run clockwise around Kalimari Desert all the time and cross the track. A kart that drives into a train is launched upward.
Weak points: The computer racers wait at the track whenever the train is on it. You can get past the train yourself by driving through the gap between two of its coaches.
Tips: How long the train is depends on the mode and the number of players. Alone, you face a coal tender pulling five passenger cars. In two-player VS the train is an engine, a tender and one passenger car. In two-player Grand Prix and in three- or four-player VS it has no tender and no passenger cars.
Tips: Nothing stops you circling the train track, but that circuit earns no lap and just sets you back.

sections.name: Giant Egg (Yoshi Valley)
sections.card:
Summary: A giant Yoshi's egg turns round and round in a big circular area near the end of Yoshi Valley, flattening whoever it meets.
Tips: After the routes come together, the winding road toward the egg has few railings.
Tips: Route 5 includes a steep 270 degree left turn crowded with porcupines; they pace back and forth and spin out a racer that runs into them.

sections.name: Chomp (Rainbow Road)
sections.card:
Summary: Several chainless Chomps sit in the middle of Rainbow Road, and a racer who hits one is thrown into the air.
Tips: In this game Rainbow Road has rails along the whole track.
Tips: No course in the game is longer: it measures 2,000 meters, and a lap takes roughly two minutes.

sections.name: Traffic (Toad's Turnpike)
sections.card:
Summary: Cars, tanker trucks, box trucks and school buses drive along Toad's Turnpike, and a racer who collides with one is knocked into the air.
Tips: Large vehicles are slow and may block your way. It is hardest on the two-lane stretches, where vehicles often run side by side and there is little room to steer through.
Tips: The road narrows to two lanes where the right U-turn begins and keeps that width all the way to the finish.
